passages.text: “Now this is the law of the guilt offering, which is most holy: The guilt offering must be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and the priest shall sprinkle its blood on all sides of the altar.
passages.sermon:
The guilt offering is most holy.
This is the law for the guilt offering.
The priest must slaughter the guilt offering in the same place as the burnt offering.
The priest must sprinkle the blood of the guilt offering on all sides of the altar.
passages.original: וְזֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הָאָשָׁ֑ם קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים הֽוּא׃ בִּמְק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁחֲטוּ֙ אֶת־ הָ֣עֹלָ֔ה יִשְׁחֲט֖וּ אֶת־ הָאָשָׁ֑ם וְאֶת־ דָּמ֛וֹ יִזְרֹ֥ק עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב׃

passages.text: And all the fat from it shall be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails, both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which is to be removed with the kidneys.
passages.sermon:
The guilt offering is a special sacrifice to God.
The priest must offer all its fat to God.
He must take the fat tail.
He must take the fat that covers the inner parts.
He must take both kidneys.
He must take the fat on the kidneys, near the loins.
He must take the lobe of the liver.
He must remove the liver lobe with the kidneys.
passages.original: וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־ חֶלְבּ֖וֹ יַקְרִ֣יב מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֵ֚ת הָֽאַלְיָ֔ה וְאֶת־ הַחֵ֖לֶב הַֽמְכַסֶּ֥ה אֶת־ הַקֶּֽרֶב׃ וְאֵת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י הַכְּלָיֹ֔ת וְאֶת־ הַחֵ֙לֶב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲלֵיהֶ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ הַכְּסָלִ֑ים וְאֶת־ הַיֹּתֶ֙רֶת֙ עַל־ הַכָּבֵ֔ד עַל־ הַכְּלָיֹ֖ת יְסִירֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: The priest shall burn them on the altar as an offering made by fire to the LORD; it is a guilt offering.
passages.sermon:
A priest serves God in the sanctuary.
The priest takes the fat parts from the guilt offering.
The priest burns these fat parts on the altar.
The fire consumes the offering on the altar.
This burning is an offering to the LORD.
This offering is called a guilt offering.
passages.original: וְהִקְטִ֨יר אֹתָ֤ם הַכֹּהֵן֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה אָשָׁ֖ם הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Every male among the priests may eat of it. It must be eaten in a holy place; it is most holy.
passages.sermon: Every male priest may eat this offering.\r\nThey must eat it in a holy place.\r\nThis offering is most holy.
passages.original: כָּל־ זָכָ֥ר בַּכֹּהֲנִ֖ים יֹאכְלֶ֑נּוּ בְּמָק֤וֹם קָדוֹשׁ֙ יֵאָכֵ֔ל קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים הֽוּא׃

passages.text: The guilt offering is like the sin offering; the same law applies to both. It belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.
passages.sermon:
The guilt offering and the sin offering are similar.
The same law applies to both offerings.
The priest makes atonement with the offering.
That offering belongs to the priest who makes atonement.
passages.original: כַּֽחַטָּאת֙ כָּֽאָשָׁ֔ם תּוֹרָ֥ה אַחַ֖ת לָהֶ֑ם הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְכַפֶּר־ בּ֖וֹ ל֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: As for the priest who presents a burnt offering for anyone, the hide of that offering belongs to him.
passages.sermon: A priest may present a burnt offering for a person.\r\nThe priest receives the hide of the burnt offering he presents.\r\nThe hide belongs to that priest.
passages.original: וְהַ֨כֹּהֵ֔ן הַמַּקְרִ֖יב אֶת־ עֹ֣לַת אִ֑ישׁ ע֤וֹר הָֽעֹלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִקְרִ֔יב לַכֹּהֵ֖ן ל֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Likewise, every grain offering that is baked in an oven or cooked in a pan or on a griddle belongs to the priest who presents it, and every grain offering, whether dry or mixed with oil, belongs equally to all the sons of Aaron.
passages.sermon:
A grain offering is a gift to God.
Some grain offerings are baked in an oven.
Some are cooked in a pan.
Some are cooked on a griddle.
The priest presents the grain offering to God.
The priest who presents the offering receives it.
Some grain offerings are mixed with oil.
Some grain offerings are dry.
All grain offerings, whether mixed with oil or dry, belong to the sons of Aaron.
Each son of Aaron receives a share, like his brother.
The sons of Aaron are the priests.
passages.original: וְכָל־ מִנְחָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר תֵּֽאָפֶה֙ בַּתַּנּ֔וּר וְכָל־ נַעֲשָׂ֥ה בַמַּרְחֶ֖שֶׁת וְעַֽל־ מַחֲבַ֑ת לַכֹּהֵ֛ן הַמַּקְרִ֥יב אֹתָ֖הּ ל֥וֹ תִֽהְיֶֽה׃ וְכָל־ מִנְחָ֥ה בְלוּלָֽה־ בַשֶּׁ֖מֶן וַחֲרֵבָ֑ה לְכָל־ בְּנֵ֧י אַהֲרֹ֛ן תִּהְיֶ֖ה אִ֥ישׁ כְּאָחִֽיו׃פ

passages.text: Now this is the law of the peace offering that one may present to the LORD: If he offers it in thanksgiving, then along with the sacrifice of thanksgiving he shall offer unleavened cakes mixed with olive oil, unleavened wafers coated with oil, and well-kneaded cakes of fine flour mixed with oil.
passages.sermon:
This is the law for the peace offering.
A person may present a peace offering to the LORD.
If a person offers the peace offering as thanksgiving, he must do the following.
He must bring unleavened cakes mixed with olive oil.
He must bring unleavened wafers coated with oil.
He must bring well-kneaded cakes made of fine flour mixed with oil.
passages.original: וְזֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת זֶ֣בַח הַשְּׁלָמִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַקְרִ֖יב לַיהוָֽה׃ אִ֣ם עַל־ תּוֹדָה֮ יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ֒ וְהִקְרִ֣יב׀ עַל־ זֶ֣בַח הַתּוֹדָ֗ה חַלּ֤וֹת מַצּוֹת֙ בְּלוּלֹ֣ת בַּשֶּׁ֔מֶן וּרְקִיקֵ֥י מַצּ֖וֹת מְשֻׁחִ֣ים בַּשָּׁ֑מֶן וְסֹ֣לֶת מֻרְבֶּ֔כֶת חַלֹּ֖ת בְּלוּלֹ֥ת בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: Along with his peace offering of thanksgiving he is to present an offering with cakes of leavened bread.
passages.sermon: A man brings a peace offering to the LORD as a thanksgiving sacrifice.\r\nHe must also bring cakes of leavened bread with his offering.\r\nHe presents these cakes together with his peace offering of thanksgiving.
passages.original: עַל־ חַלֹּת֙ לֶ֣חֶם חָמֵ֔ץ יַקְרִ֖יב קָרְבָּנ֑וֹ עַל־ זֶ֖בַח תּוֹדַ֥ת שְׁלָמָֽיו׃

passages.text: From the cakes he must present one portion of each offering as a contribution to the LORD. It belongs to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering.
passages.sermon:
The person brings a peace offering to the LORD.
He must also bring cakes with the offering.
He must take one cake from each kind of offering.
He gives this one cake as a contribution to the LORD.
This cake belongs to the priest.
The priest sprinkles the blood of the peace offering.
The priest receives the cake.
passages.original: וְהִקְרִ֨יב מִמֶּ֤נּוּ אֶחָד֙ מִכָּל־ קָרְבָּ֔ן תְּרוּמָ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה לַכֹּהֵ֗ן הַזֹּרֵ֛ק אֶת־ דַּ֥ם הַשְּׁלָמִ֖ים ל֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: The meat of the sacrifice of his peace offering of thanksgiving must be eaten on the day he offers it; none of it may be left until morning.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions for peace offerings of thanksgiving.
A person must offer a sacrifice to God.
The sacrifice includes meat.
The person must eat the meat on the same day he offers the sacrifice.
He must not leave any of the meat until the next morning.
passages.original: וּבְשַׂ֗ר זֶ֚בַח תּוֹדַ֣ת שְׁלָמָ֔יו בְּי֥וֹם קָרְבָּנ֖וֹ יֵאָכֵ֑ל לֹֽא־ יַנִּ֥יחַ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד־ בֹּֽקֶר׃

passages.text: If, however, the sacrifice he offers is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, but the remainder may be eaten on the next day.
passages.sermon:
A man brings a sacrifice to the LORD.
He may bring it as a vow.
He may bring it as a freewill offering.
He must eat the sacrifice on the day he offers it.
If any meat remains, he may eat the rest on the next day.
passages.original: וְאִם־ נֶ֣דֶר׀ א֣וֹ נְדָבָ֗ה זֶ֚בַח קָרְבָּנ֔וֹ בְּי֛וֹם הַקְרִיב֥וֹ אֶת־ זִבְח֖וֹ יֵאָכֵ֑ל וּמִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וְהַנּוֹתָ֥ר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ יֵאָכֵֽל׃

passages.text: But any meat of the sacrifice remaining until the third day must be burned up.
passages.sermon:
This law speaks about the meat from a sacrifice.
The sacrifice is an offering to God.
If any meat from the sacrifice remains until the third day, you must not eat it.
You must burn the leftover meat with fire on the third day.
passages.original: וְהַנּוֹתָ֖ר מִבְּשַׂ֣ר הַזָּ֑בַח בַּיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י בָּאֵ֖שׁ יִשָּׂרֵֽף׃

passages.text: If any of the meat from his peace offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not be credited to the one who presented it; it shall be an abomination, and the one who eats of it shall bear his iniquity.
passages.sermon:
A man brings a peace offering to the LORD.
If anyone eats any of the meat from this offering on the third day, God will not accept it.
God will not count this offering for the person who brought it.
This meat will be considered defiled.
Anyone who eats this meat will be guilty.
That person will bear his own sin.
passages.original: וְאִ֣ם הֵאָכֹ֣ל יֵ֠אָכֵל מִבְּשַׂר־ זֶ֨בַח שְׁלָמָ֜יו בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי֮ לֹ֣א יֵרָצֶה֒ הַמַּקְרִ֣יב אֹת֗וֹ לֹ֧א יֵחָשֵׁ֛ב ל֖וֹ פִּגּ֣וּל יִהְיֶ֑ה וְהַנֶּ֛פֶשׁ הָאֹכֶ֥לֶת מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עֲוֺנָ֥הּ תִּשָּֽׂא׃

passages.text: Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten; it is to be burned up. As for any other meat, anyone who is ceremonially clean may eat it.
passages.sermon:
Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten.
Burn this meat in the fire.
Meat that is clean may be eaten.
Anyone who is ceremonially clean may eat this meat.
passages.original: וְהַבָּשָׂ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־ יִגַּ֤ע בְּכָל־ טָמֵא֙ לֹ֣א יֵֽאָכֵ֔ל בָּאֵ֖שׁ יִשָּׂרֵ֑ף וְהַ֨בָּשָׂ֔ר כָּל־ טָה֖וֹר יֹאכַ֥ל בָּשָֽׂר׃

passages.text: But if anyone who is unclean eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave rules to the Israelites about peace offerings.
A peace offering is a sacrifice that belongs to the LORD.
A person may be unclean for many reasons.
If a person is unclean, that person must not eat meat from the peace offering.
If an unclean person eats this meat, that person breaks God's command.
God says that person must be cut off from his people.
passages.original: וְהַנֶּ֜פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־ תֹּאכַ֣ל בָּשָׂ֗ר מִזֶּ֤בַח הַשְּׁלָמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַיהוָ֔ה וְטֻמְאָת֖וֹ עָלָ֑יו וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵעַמֶּֽיהָ׃

passages.text: If one touches anything unclean, whether human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean, detestable thing, and then eats any of the meat of the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.”
passages.sermon:
A person may become unclean.
A person becomes unclean by touching anything unclean.
Unclean things include human uncleanness.
Unclean things include unclean animals.
Unclean things include any unclean, detestable thing.
If a person is unclean and eats meat from the peace offering,
This peace offering belongs to the LORD.
That person must be cut off from his people.
passages.original: וְנֶ֜פֶשׁ כִּֽי־ תִגַּ֣ע בְּכָל־ טָמֵ֗א בְּטֻמְאַ֤ת אָדָם֙ א֣וֹ׀ בִּבְהֵמָ֣ה טְמֵאָ֗ה א֚וֹ בְּכָל־ שֶׁ֣קֶץ טָמֵ֔א וְאָכַ֛ל מִבְּשַׂר־ זֶ֥בַח הַשְּׁלָמִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַיהוָ֑ה וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵעַמֶּֽיהָ׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘You are not to eat any of the fat of an ox, a sheep, or a goat.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
The LORD said to the Israelites, “Do not eat any fat.
Do not eat the fat of an ox.
Do not eat the fat of a sheep.
Do not eat the fat of a goat.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כָּל־ חֵ֜לֶב שׁ֥וֹר וְכֶ֛שֶׂב וָעֵ֖ז לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: The fat of an animal found dead or mauled by wild beasts may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it.
passages.sermon:
God gave a law to the Israelites.
God spoke through Moses.
God said, “You may use the fat of an animal that died on its own for any purpose.
You may use the fat of an animal killed by wild beasts for any purpose.
But you must not eat this fat.”
passages.original: וְחֵ֤לֶב נְבֵלָה֙ וְחֵ֣לֶב טְרֵפָ֔ה יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה לְכָל־ מְלָאכָ֑ה וְאָכֹ֖ל לֹ֥א תֹאכְלֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: If anyone eats the fat of an animal from which an offering made by fire may be presented to the LORD, the one who eats it must be cut off from his people.
passages.sermon:
God gave a law to the Israelites through Moses.
God said this law to Moses.
If a person eats the fat of an animal,
and that animal is one that people may offer to the LORD as a burnt offering,
then that person must be cut off from his people.
passages.original: כִּ֚י כָּל־ אֹכֵ֣ל חֵ֔לֶב מִן־ הַ֨בְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְרִ֥יב מִמֶּ֛נָּה אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הָאֹכֶ֖לֶת מֵֽעַמֶּֽיהָ׃

passages.text: You must not eat the blood of any bird or animal in any of your dwellings.
passages.sermon:
God gave a command to the Israelites.
God said, “Do not eat blood.
Do not eat the blood of any bird.
Do not eat the blood of any animal.
Do not eat blood in any of your homes.
Obey this command wherever you live.”
passages.original: וְכָל־ דָּם֙ לֹ֣א תֹאכְל֔וּ בְּכֹ֖ל מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶ֑ם לָע֖וֹף וְלַבְּהֵמָֽה׃

passages.text: If anyone eats blood, that person must be cut off from his people.’ ”
passages.sermon: God gave a command to the Israelites.\r\nGod said, “If any person eats blood, that person must be cut off from his people.”
passages.original: כָּל־ נֶ֖פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־ תֹּאכַ֣ל כָּל־ דָּ֑ם וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵֽעַמֶּֽיהָ׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘Anyone who presents a peace offering to the LORD must bring it as his sacrifice to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
The LORD said, “Anyone who brings a peace offering to the LORD must bring his sacrifice to the LORD.
The person must bring the offering as a peace offering to the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הַמַּקְרִ֞יב אֶת־ זֶ֤בַח שְׁלָמָיו֙ לַיהוָ֔ה יָבִ֧יא אֶת־ קָרְבָּנ֛וֹ לַיהוָ֖ה מִזֶּ֥בַח שְׁלָמָֽיו׃

passages.text: With his own hands he is to bring the offerings made by fire to the LORD; he shall bring the fat, together with the breast, and wave the breast as a wave offering before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A man brings a peace offering to the LORD.
He must bring the offering himself.
He uses his own hands.
He brings the fat to the LORD.
He brings the breast with the fat.
He waves the breast before the LORD.
He offers the breast as a wave offering.
passages.original: יָדָ֣יו תְּבִיאֶ֔ינָה אֵ֖ת אִשֵּׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֶת־ הַחֵ֤לֶב עַל־ הֶֽחָזֶה֙ יְבִיאֶ֔נּוּ אֵ֣ת הֶחָזֶ֗ה לְהָנִ֥יף אֹת֛וֹ תְּנוּפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The priest is to burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
passages.sermon: The priest burns the fat on the altar.\r\nThe breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
passages.original: וְהִקְטִ֧יר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת־ הַחֵ֖לֶב הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חָה וְהָיָה֙ הֶֽחָזֶ֔ה לְאַהֲרֹ֖ן וּלְבָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: And you are to give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your peace offering.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel instructions for peace offerings.
God commanded the people to give a portion to the priest.
You must give the right thigh to the priest.
This right thigh is a contribution.
You take it from your peace offering.
passages.original: וְאֵת֙ שׁ֣וֹק הַיָּמִ֔ין תִּתְּנ֥וּ תְרוּמָ֖ה לַכֹּהֵ֑ן מִזִּבְחֵ֖י שַׁלְמֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: The son of Aaron who presents the blood and fat of the peace offering shall have the right thigh as a portion.
passages.sermon:
Aaron was the first high priest of Israel.
Aaron had sons who served as priests.
A son of Aaron may present a peace offering.
A peace offering includes blood and fat.
A son of Aaron who presents the blood and fat of the peace offering receives a portion.
The right thigh is that portion.
The right thigh belongs to the son of Aaron who presents the blood and fat.
passages.original: הַמַּקְרִ֞יב אֶת־ דַּ֧ם הַשְּׁלָמִ֛ים וְאֶת־ הַחֵ֖לֶב מִבְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֑ן ל֧וֹ תִהְיֶ֛ה שׁ֥וֹק הַיָּמִ֖ין לְמָנָֽה׃

passages.text: I have taken from the sons of Israel the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution of their peace offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a permanent portion from the sons of Israel.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions to the people of Israel.
God took the breast of the wave offering from the Israelites.
God also took the thigh of the contribution from their peace offerings.
God gave these parts to Aaron the priest and to his sons.
God made this a permanent portion for Aaron and his sons.
God commanded the Israelites to give these portions.
passages.original: כִּי֩ אֶת־ חֲזֵ֨ה הַתְּנוּפָ֜ה וְאֵ֣ת׀ שׁ֣וֹק הַתְּרוּמָ֗ה לָקַ֙חְתִּי֙ מֵאֵ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִזִּבְחֵ֖י שַׁלְמֵיהֶ֑ם וָאֶתֵּ֣ן אֹ֠תָם לְאַהֲרֹ֨ן הַכֹּהֵ֤ן וּלְבָנָיו֙ לְחָק־ עוֹלָ֔ם מֵאֵ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: This is the portion of the offerings made by fire to the LORD for Aaron and his sons since the day they were presented to serve the LORD as priests.
passages.sermon:
Aaron was the first high priest of Israel.
Aaron had sons who also served as priests.
The LORD gave special offerings to Aaron and his sons.
These offerings were made by fire to the LORD.
Aaron and his sons received their portion from these offerings.
They began to receive this portion on the day they were presented as priests.
They served the LORD as priests from that day.
passages.original: זֹ֣את מִשְׁחַ֤ת אַהֲרֹן֙ וּמִשְׁחַ֣ת בָּנָ֔יו מֵאִשֵּׁ֖י יְהוָ֑ה בְּיוֹם֙ הִקְרִ֣יב אֹתָ֔ם לְכַהֵ֖ן לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: On the day they were anointed, the LORD commanded that this be given them by the sons of Israel. It is a permanent portion for the generations to come.
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave a command.
He commanded the sons of Israel to give a portion to Aaron and his sons.
This command was given on the day Aaron and his sons were anointed as priests.
This portion is permanent.
This rule will last for all generations.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁר֩ צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה לָתֵ֣ת לָהֶ֗ם בְּיוֹם֙ מָשְׁח֣וֹ אֹתָ֔ם מֵאֵ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the peace offering, which the LORD gave Moses on Mount Sinai on the day He commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai.
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave laws to Moses on Mount Sinai.
The LORD told Moses about offerings.
These offerings are the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the peace offering.
The LORD commanded the Israelites to bring these offerings to Him.
The LORD gave this command in the Wilderness of Sinai.
passages.original: זֹ֣את הַתּוֹרָ֗ה לָֽעֹלָה֙ לַמִּנְחָ֔ה וְלַֽחַטָּ֖את וְלָאָשָׁ֑ם וְלַ֨מִּלּוּאִ֔ים וּלְזֶ֖בַח הַשְּׁלָמִֽים׃ אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּהַ֣ר סִינָ֑י בְּי֨וֹם צַוֺּת֜וֹ אֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְהַקְרִ֧יב אֶת־ קָרְבְּנֵיהֶ֛ם לַיהוָ֖ה בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי׃פ
